name_note: provider agency / source-role test (NOT agent-vs-instrument: instruments are never modeled as providers; agency of the subject provider varies)
motivation: eight single-factor probes show no systematic silence effect; moving from surface/syntax factors to semantic role representation

hypothesis.H1: Candidate Generation shows higher TRUE-SILENCE rates for non-agentive source providers than for agentive providers, given identical frame/recipient/theme.
hypothesis.H0: TRUE-SILENCE rate does not depend on provider agency.

frame: ditransitive Provider + provides + Recipient + Theme; theme domains varied (information, medical, physical, service/output) and documented per item, not confounded with class
gold: all YES items are provides (agency varies, relation constant); NO mirrors use deny
primary_endpoint: TRUE_SILENCE = expected_candidate true AND candidate_absent, per class
outcome_separation_note: no correct triple is not automatically silence (cf. OIE error classes: missing extraction vs wrong arguments vs wrong boundaries)
decision_rule: H1 supported ONLY by a clearly elevated TRUE-SILENCE rate in non-agentive source classes vs agentive controls. A single miss is an item finding (e.g. R-classes 16/16, 16/16, 15/16, 16/16 does NOT confirm H1).
material_shape: 16 pairs (4 per class) x YES/NO with deny = 32 sentences
test_material: built by script; validation + freeze below
